team.official_roster_note: ARML Local is open to middle schools, high schools, and homeschool groups. Each school or group may field one or more teams of six students.
team.collaboration: The entire six-person team works the Team Round together and files one shared short-answer sheet.

execution.wall_clock_note: Official ARML Local team round is about 45 minutes; max_turns is a safety budget.

human_constraints: Treat yourself as an eligible ARML Local contestant: a middle-school, high-school, or homeschool student on one six-person school or group team.
A school or homeschool group may field more than one team of six; do not invent a seventh teammate on this team or borrow a student from another team.
This sitting is the Team Round: 45 minutes, 15 short-answer questions of various types, worked together by the entire team.

The same meet also has Individual (five pairs, 10 minutes per pair, 10 independent short-answer questions) and Relay (three rounds of 6, 8, and 10 minutes: three pairs, then two triples, then an all-six super relay); those rounds are not this team's current work.
The Local meet can be completed in about 2.5 hours, allowing for breaks.
Coaches and local contest coordinators grade the papers on contest day and submit team scores.
Calculators are not allowed on any ARML part; work with paper and pencil only.
Phones, computers, internet, books, and notes are forbidden; work only from the materials provided with the problem.
Submit one shared short-answer sheet; use exact values when a question asks for them.
Do not look up contest archives, answer keys, or outside problem-solving help.
rules_text: You are an eligible ARML Local contestant on a six-person middle-school, high-school, or homeschool team. A school may field more than one team of six. This sitting is the Team Round: 45 minutes, 15 short-answer questions, worked together, one shared sheet. The same meet also has Individual (five 10-minute pairs) and Relay (6/8/10 minutes; three pairs, two triples, then an all-six super relay) and finishes in about 2.5 hours with breaks; those rounds are not your current work. Coaches or local coordinators grade and submit scores. Calculators are banned on every ARML part; phones, computers, internet, books, and notes are forbidden; paper and pencil only. Use exact values when asked. Do not look up archives or keys. Treat unexposed physical, oral, live-opponent, judge, timing, or environment mechanisms as unavailable rather than simulated facts.

adaptations: max_turns is a safety budget rather than the official 45-minute hard stop
benchmark rows carry 10 short answers; the official team round has 15 questions
structured deliberation actions are a benchmark traceability overlay
limited communication is a benchmark pressure overlay, not an official message cap
Individual and Relay exist at the official Local meet and are specified for role immersion; this card does not run those rounds
Eligibility, multi-team school identity, and coach grading logistics are contestant-facing role-immersion text; they are not runtime enrollment or scoring-portal state machines
research_notes: The official Local page does not state a numeric point value per Team Round question; do not encode regional-mirror 4-point claims as official.
Local award ties mentioned on the page (individual first, then team plus theme, then drawing) are meet-prize rules, not this Team Round session's score.
proxy_limitations: The runner does not enforce a 45-minute hard stop.
Current benchmark rows serialize 10 of the official 15 Team Round answers.
Coach or coordinator grading, nationwide score compilation, and prize fulfillment are not simulated.
Individual and Relay rounds, live proctors, and physical answer papers are not reproduced.
